milestones.title: Pizarro founds the Ciudad de los Reyes
milestones.detail: Francisco Pizarro founded the city on 18 January 1535 beside the Rímac river, on land administered by the local curaca Taulichusco.

milestones.title: Capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru
milestones.detail: Lima became the capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru and the seat of a Real Audiencia in 1543.

milestones.title: University of San Marcos founded
milestones.detail: The University of San Marcos was founded in 1551.

milestones.title: City walls completed
milestones.detail: The Walls of Lima, with bastions and ten gates, were built between 1684 and 1687 under Viceroy Melchor de Navarra y Rocafull to defend the city against pirates.

milestones.title: Earthquake destroys Lima and Callao
milestones.detail: On 28 October 1746 a powerful earthquake severely damaged the city and destroyed Callao, forcing a massive rebuilding effort under Viceroy José Antonio Manso de Velasco.

milestones.title: Independence proclaimed
milestones.detail: José de San Martín's forces took Lima in 1821 and Peruvian independence from Spain was declared.

milestones.title: Lima–Callao railway
milestones.detail: A railway line between Lima and its port of Callao was completed in 1850.

milestones.title: City walls demolished
milestones.detail: The colonial walls were torn down to make room for urban growth (sources date the demolition between 1870 and 1872).

milestones.title: Chilean occupation
milestones.detail: During the War of the Pacific the Chilean army occupied Lima in 1881 after defeating Peruvian forces in the battles of San Juan and Miraflores.

milestones.title: Mass migration from the Andes begins
milestones.detail: From the 1940s Lima grew rapidly through migration from the Andean regions; the 1940 census counted 562,885 people in the province, and land invasions later produced the barriadas or pueblos jóvenes.
milestones.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Lima; INEI, Perfil Sociodemográfico de la Provincia de Lima (Censos Nacionales 2007), cuadro 1.1, https://www.inei.gob.pe/media/MenuRecursivo/publicaciones_digitales/Est/Lib0838/Libro15/cap01.pdf

milestones.title: Historic centre inscribed by UNESCO
milestones.detail: The Historic Centre of Lima, covering parts of the districts of Lima and Rímac, was declared a World Heritage Site in 1988.

milestones.title: Metropolitano bus rapid transit opens
milestones.detail: El Metropolitano bus transit system began operating in 2010.

milestones.title: Metro Line 1 enters revenue service
milestones.detail: Line 1 of the Lima and Callao Metro, whose first section had been completed in 1990, began revenue service on 11 April 2011.

notes: Start date: the Spanish foundation of the Ciudad de los Reyes on 18 January 1535 is used and is not contested as the founding of the city itself. The site was already inhabited: this part of the Rímac valley was administered by the curaca Taulichusco, and much older adobe monuments (huacas such as Huaca Pucllana, of the Lima culture, 200-700 CE) survive inside the modern metropolis. Under the brief's rule these earlier valley settlements are treated as predecessors on the site rather than as the city, so the clock starts in 1535; a reader who counts continuous occupation of the site would start many centuries earlier. No landmark is entered for the huacas because no sourced height was found. Population: there is no figure between the founding and 1600. Colonial values to 1790 are the city counts in the Compendio de Historia Económica del Perú as published by the central bank (the 1746 and 1755 values are round estimates either side of the earthquake). The definition then changes: 1836 is Chandler's city figure, and from 1862 the series is the province of Lima (city plus surrounding valley districts, excluding Callao), because that is the only consistent run found from 1862 to 1940; the city-only figures for 1876 and 1908 are given in the point notes and are about 15-20 per cent lower. The UN series from 1950 measures the Lima-Callao agglomeration, so a further small definitional step occurs there. Not used: 63,900 for 1812 (Marley, via Wikipedia) against Chandler's 56,284 for 1813; 85,116, which the Compendio dates to 1850 for the Cercado and Chandler to 1856; and the Compendio's 251,519 for 1931, which is hard to reconcile with the 1920 and 1940 values. No other 1931 figure was found on an open page, so there is a gap between 1920 and 1940. Landmarks: the list is weak before 1956. Heights could not be sourced for the Cathedral, the Basilica of San Francisco, the Government Palace, Torre Tagle, the Real Felipe fortress in Callao, the Gran Hotel Bolívar or the Palacio de Justicia, so colonial and republican Lima is represented only by the Santo Domingo tower, for which two press sources disagree (52 m and 46 m). Modern heights and years are from CTBUH; CTBUH lists Torre Rímac (208 m) only as proposed.
